name: thefirestore-failure-case
description: DELIBERATE FAILURE CASE: nine Button modifiers modeled as nine separate components. This is the shape of output when an extraction pipeline observes .button--primary, .button--secondary, .button--tertiary, .button--accent, .button--large, .button--small, .button--slab, .button--icon, and .button--inputAction as sibling selectors and has no principled way to decide which are color-axis variants, which are size-axis variants, which are state modifiers, and which are distinct components entirely.
ambiguityNote: Contrast with bungee-pro's failure-case: there, the ambiguity was 'are .button-primary and .button-primary-v2 one component or two?' (identical styles, different names). Here, the ambiguity is 'which of these nine --modifier classes are axes of a single component, which are states, and which are distinct primitives?' (distinct styles, shared prefix). Both problems require semantic judgment. Neither is solved by style-signature equivalence. An automated pipeline running a clustering step would either (a) merge too aggressively into one Button component and lose the semantic distinctions, or (b) split too aggressively like this registry and produce a maintenance nightmare where 'make all primary buttons use rounded-lg' requires editing nine files.

components.name: ButtonLarge
components.description: The .button--large modifier, treated as its own component. Note: this is a size modifier, not a color modifier — a clustering pipeline that can't distinguish axes merges it with the color variants.

components.name: ButtonSmall
components.description: The .button--small modifier. Also a size-axis modifier.

components.name: ButtonInputAction
components.description: The .button--inputAction modifier. Specialized component attached to input fields — declared style is transparent, borderless, with a negative margin to overlay the input. Semantically distinct from other Button modifiers despite sharing the .button-- prefix.
